subtopics.title: The Circular Flow, the Multiplier and Business Cycles

questions.question: In the open circular-flow model, the economy is in equilibrium when:
options: Leakages equal injections — savings plus taxes plus imports equal investment plus government spending plus exports

questions.question: Households spend 0,75 of each extra rand. The multiplier is:
options: Four — one divided by the 0,25 that is not spent

questions.question: The three methods of measuring GDP are:
Keynesians differ from monetarists on business cycles because Keynesians:
options: See causes inside the economy — swings of confidence and spending — and want the state to lean against them

subtopics.title: The Public Sector, the Budget and Fiscal Policy

questions.question: The five macro objectives of the public sector are growth, full employment, price stability, economic equity and:
options: Exchange rate stability with external balance

questions.question: The rolling three-year spending plan, as against the October mid-year update, is:
On the Laffer curve, revenue is zero at BOTH extremes because:
options: The curve is drawn upside down
At nought percent nothing is collected, and at one hundred percent effort loses all reward

questions.question: Bureaucracy, political interference and special interest groups are listed causes of:
options: Public sector failure — good intentions misfiring in delivery

subtopics.title: Foreign Exchange Markets and the Balance of Payments

questions.question: A foreigner buying shares on the South African exchange is recorded as:
options: Portfolio investment in the financial account

questions.question: South Africans import more goods. On the foreign exchange market this:
options: Shifts the supply of foreign currency right
Shifts the demand for foreign currency right, so the rand depreciates
Has no effect on the rand

questions.question: Devaluation and revaluation, as against depreciation and appreciation, belong to:
The terms of trade are calculated as:
options: The repo rate times one hundred
The index of export prices divided by the index of import prices, times one hundred

subtopics.title: Economic Pursuits: Trade Policy, Growth and Indicators

questions.question: Sheltering home industries behind tariffs and quotas so they can replace imports is:
Growth, as against development, is best defined as:
options: The increase in real GDP, while development widens living standards, capabilities and choices
The same thing by another name

questions.question: The national plan aiming at 2030 is:
Life expectancy, clean water access and school enrolment are examples of:

subtopics.title: Round and Round: The Economy as One Big Taxi Route

questions.question: In the taxi-route picture, money saved, taxed or spent on imports is:
options: A leakage — passengers leaving the route

questions.question: A firm spends R8 million on a depot and people spend 75 cents of every rand. Total income around town eventually rises by:
options: R32 million — the multiplier of four at work

questions.question: The busy season, the peak, the quiet months and the trough, around a rising trend, describe:

subtopics.title: The Nation's Purse and the Price of the Rand

questions.question: The three biggest sources filling the nation's purse are:
options: Personal income tax, value-added tax and company tax
The repo rate, bonds and levies

questions.question: The tuckshop version of the Laffer curve teaches that:
options: Higher prices always raise more money
Both a price of nothing and a price nobody pays leave the till empty — the best rate lies between
The till fills fastest at a hundred percent

questions.question: At the rand's street stall, foreign money gets more expensive when:
options: Exporters flood the stall with foreign money
Buyers of foreign money crowd the stall while sellers are few — the rand weakens

questions.question: The balanced evaluation of a weak rand is that:
options: Exports and tourism win while petrol and imported medicine cost more — hold both sides

subtopics.title: Growing the Pie: Trade, Plans and Report Cards

questions.question: In the school-shoes debate, a levy on imported shoes:
options: Keeps the cobbler's jobs local while every family pays more — protection's two sides
Has no effect on the cobbler

questions.question: Growth without development means:
options: The pie shrinks while everyone eats
Income climbs while the same families stay hungry — a bigger pie, not more eaters

questions.question: Coastal industrial zones and cross-border corridors are attempts to:
options: Carry the ovens to where the unemployed already live — moving industry to people

questions.question: The report-card habit that earns evaluation marks is:
options: Comparing no more than two towns
Never judging one column alone — the card only makes sense read whole
